name: pip
description: Historical non-security requirement-parsing bug: a wheel filename followed by whitespace and an extras list is interpreted as a package name instead of a wheel requirement. The upstream fix was authored on 2025-08-04 and merged in PR #13523 on 2025-09-11. The base is its immediate parent. regression.patch contains exactly the one regression parameter added upstream; repair.patch contains exactly the upstream source diff, without its news fragment.
question: A wheel requirement such as 'simple-0.1-py2.py3-none-any.whl [ext]' must identify project simple at version 0.1 and preserve the requested extras. Dropping its extras must produce 'simple==0.1'. Currently the filename is interpreted as a package name. Correct requirement parsing while preserving existing behavior for other requirement forms.
evidence: 1 failed, 80 passed, 3 skipped, 3 deselected, 3 warnings in 1.32s
license: MIT; upstream copyright and license are reproduced in LICENSE.txt.

validation.selection_basis: First serious candidate. Selected for a clear documented contract, a minimal genuine upstream regression, Python 3.12 compatibility, and fast offline reproduction. Test selection was based on requirement construction and InstallRequirement behavior, not output volume.

suite.rationale: Complete related unit modules cover parsing requirements, extras, local paths, wheel requirements, and InstallRequirement construction. The upstream regression is included once in both diagnostic_args and verify_args. It was also run independently for failure/pass attribution.
suite.network_restriction_reason: These existing upstream network-marked tests fetch PyPI packages, a GitHub archive, or a remote VCS checkout. Exclusion is required independently of the defect by the offline execution contract.
suite.automatic_platform_skips: The three parameters of tests/unit/test_req.py::test_looks_like_path_win retain the upstream skipif(not sys.platform.startswith('win')) decorator and its 'Test only available on Windows' reason.
suite.configuration: Unmodified upstream pyproject.toml and conftest.py. pytest-subket remains active with upstream socket restrictions. --color=no changes presentation only. No test/configuration rewrites, duplicate tests, artificial output, or new skip rules.

platform.workspace_pip_version_note: The pip==25.1.1 distribution in the venv is only the pinned bootstrap installer. Tests import the archived upstream pip source through PYTHONPATH, verified explicitly for pip.__file__ and constructors.__file__.

validation.dependency_release_evidence: First upload dates and dependency metadata were checked at https://pypi.org/pypi/{distribution}/{version}/json for each exact pin. All selected releases predate validation by more than seven days. setup.sh uses binary-only, no-deps installation of all direct and transitive requirements. No source build is needed.

archive_contract.reuse: The initial base setup created the venv. Fixed and oracle workspaces reused it with networking unavailable via unshare -Urn. pip freeze --all remained byte-identical before and after both reuse calls; setup checked exact installed versions instead of reinstalling them.
archive_contract.workspace_preparation: setup.sh copies cached pinned setuptools and wheel wheels into each workspace's tests/data/common_wheels for offline fixture builds. No pip project installation, editable installation, or generated project metadata is required by the selected modules.
archive_contract.fixed_workspace_procedure: Archive the broken parent, apply regression.patch, call setup.sh with the reused venv, freeze baseline SHA-256 hashes, then apply repair.patch. All preexisting baseline files except the sole editable source file retained their hashes after tests.
archive_contract.oracle_workspace_procedure: Create another fresh parent archive, apply only regression.patch, reuse setup offline, and freeze baseline SHA-256 hashes. Copy only src/pip/_internal/req/constructors.py from the repaired workspace, without copying repair.patch. verify_args passed, and all other preexisting baseline files retained their hashes.
archive_contract.source_integrity: setup.sh asserts pip.__file__ and constructors.__file__ resolve to the supplied workspace/src paths on every call. The patched test file was byte-compared against the fix commit; broken source was byte-compared against the parent; repaired source was byte-compared against the fix commit. The fix is an ancestor of upstream origin/main.
archive_contract.offline_enforcement: All seven test runs used timeout 120s unshare -Urn with the case environment, so subprocesses also had no external network. PIP_NO_INDEX and cached build wheels permit normal offline builds. pytest-subket's upstream socket guard remains enabled.

commands.variables: Set WORKSPACE to the run's recorded workspace, VENV=/home/ubuntu/pip-validation/venv, and PACKAGE=/home/ubuntu/repos/jev-pruner/evals/historical/pip. Run pytest from WORKSPACE with the case environment expanded for that workspace.
commands.diagnostic: timeout 120s unshare -Urn "$VENV/bin/python" -m pytest -vv --color=no -m 'not network' tests/unit/test_req.py tests/unit/test_req_install.py
commands.verify: timeout 120s unshare -Urn "$VENV/bin/python" -m pytest -q --color=no -m 'not network' tests/unit/test_req.py tests/unit/test_req_install.py
commands.measurement: /usr/bin/time -f 'exit=%x elapsed_seconds=%e' -o RUN.time COMMAND > RUN.log 2>&1; output_characters is wc -m < RUN.log, without the separate time file.

known_gaps: Only the complete related requirement and install-requirement unit modules were selected; the full pip repository suite and installation CLI integration suite were not run.
Three upstream network-marked tests are intentionally deselected. Three existing Windows-only parameter cases automatically skip on Linux.
Three preexisting deprecation warnings occur in both whole-module runs and are retained.
Natural verbose diagnostic output is only 12,158 characters broken and 10,369 characters repaired. It was neither padded nor used to choose the defect or suite.
Timing and output length vary with machine speed and absolute workspace paths.
Validation used Linux CPython 3.12.13; other operating systems and Python versions were not evaluated.
